item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact requested API using FilesOption and multipartbody.NewFile, preserves existing option semantics, and provides strong coverage for multipart encoding, retries, validation, and reader failures. Neither patch routes Upload through FilesService.Add, but A additionally introduces explicitly forbidden APIs and machinery.","reasons":["B implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead invents AddFileOption, breaking contract fidelity and preventing existing FilesOption use.","B directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile as required. A adds NewFileWithFields and sorting machinery that the contract neither needs nor permits.","A adds deal/person/organization/product/activity/project/lead association options despite the explicit instruction not to add association fields.","B preserves FilesOption query and request-option behavior; its test verifies an existing request option reaches Upload. A creates duplicate option-processing infrastructure instead of reusing the established pattern and changes the convenience API's option type semantics entirely. Both duplicate Add's final request/response logic rather than calling Add, which is the principal defect in B as well as A, but B's duplicated path at least closely mirrors Add's behavior while A adds query/form-field complexity around it, increasing divergence risk and review surface. B tests all requested dimensions, including a source-reader failure before transport, full bodies on both retry attempts for Files.Add, multipart field/name/content, and validation. A lacks a direct Upload source-reader-error test and its retry assertions generally retain only the last body rather than proving both attempts received the full payload. B's replay buffering propagates io.ReadAll failures with context. A's makeBodyReplayable silently ignores read failures after consuming some or all of req.Body, potentially sending an exhausted or truncated body and losing the source error."],"risks_a":["The public Upload API is contract-incompatible because it accepts AddFileOption rather than FilesOption.","Forbidden association fields and several new exported option functions unnecessarily expand the SDK API.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, duplicating request construction, decoding, and error handling instead of retaining one implementation path. makeBodyReplayable suppresses read errors and can proceed with a damaged body. It buffers every otherwise non-replayable RawClient body even when retries are disabled, broadening behavior and memory use beyond necessity. The multipart helper and deterministic-field machinery are unnecessary repository churn."],"risks_b":["Upload still calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, so future Add changes may diverge and the contract's single-path requirement is unmet.","The RawClient-wide buffering change expands scope beyond file uploads and changes memory behavior for arbitrary reader bodies whenever per-request retries are not disabled.","Documentation claims WithNoRetry avoids buffering, but callers cannot avoid buffering merely because the configured retry policy would not retry that method; the check only observes the per-request override."]}
